question: Regulation (EU) 2026/6871 defines its scope as agricultural products under the World Trade Organization Agreement on Agriculture, which excludes fish and fish products, and no fishery or aquaculture product appears in its list of sensitive products. EU tariffs on Mercosur hake and squid were eliminated as soon as the agreement began to apply, and tariffs on shrimp are being phased out within a few years, none of which are cushioned by a tariff-rate quota. 1.

Does the Commission confirm that fishery and aquaculture products fall outside Regulation (EU) 2026/687, and that bilateral safeguards for them are instead governed by Regulation (EU) 2019/2872, as amended to cover the EU-Mercosur Agreement?

Given that the EU’s market observatories for agricultural products do not cover these products, how does the Commission monitor import volumes and prices for Mercosur fishery and aquaculture products, and will it report on them to Parliament?

Since Regulation (EU) 2019/287 provides for investigations within six months, extendable by three, and only an annual report to Parliament, without the automatic thresholds available for sensitive agricultural products, does the Commission consider that this gives EU aquaculture producers protection as swift as that provided for producers of sensitive agricultural products?

Regulation (EU) 2026/687 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 March 2026 implementing the bilateral safeguard clauses of the EU-Mercosur Partnership Agreement and the EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement for agricultural products, (OJ L, 2026/687, 19.3.2026, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/687/oj).

2 Regulation (EU) 2019/287 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 13 February 2019 implementing bilateral safeguard clauses and other mechanisms allowing for the temporary withdrawal of preferences in certain trade agreements concluded between the European Union and third countries, (OJ L 53, 22.2.2019, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2019/287/oj). 1
